english.title: Transport animals in England in way that causes injury/suffering
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) **(..SPECIFY DETAILS OF THE OFFENCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to Article 5(1)(a) of the Welfare of Animals (Transport) (England) Order 2006 and sections 73 and 75 of the Animal Health Act 1981.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
without lawful authority or excuse
transported an animal
in a way which caused or was likely to cause injury or unnecessary suffering to that animal

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: The definition of 'animal' is extended to cover all vertebrate animals and cold-blooded invertebrate animals in Article 3 of the Welfare of Animals (Transport) (England) Order 2006.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and/or fine not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions
Complex - see section 71A of the Animal Health Act 1981

Note
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' Court was removed - as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
